justification: REVERT. THE BOUND IS BREACHED: the frozen prediction (prediction.json sha c99260f031c991fccbc7a506033cc5a1b89dd90f2e9951e417708587fb621923) pre-registered max_regressions = 0 as this cycle's falsifiable bound. The blinded flip-adjudicator seat returned 5 regressions over the 18 measured flips; a split-blind frontier verification leg, blind to the first leg's verdicts, CONFIRMED 4 of them bidirectionally (m0239, m0275, m0466, m0018), split on m0108 (recorded CONTESTED, final `unclear`, both reasons preserved), and judged m0355 correct (leg 1 unclear) — so the pre-registered threshold-proximity case is NOT a regression. At the strict two-leg count of 4, and at the driver's mechanical count of 5, the bound fires either way. DOCUMENT-SIDE GROUNDS, citing flip adjudications only: the configuration removes clauses an auditor of these behaviours needs — the document's one de-radicalization directive (m0239), its record of how to respond to a user announcing intent to shoot someone (m0275), its anthrax-request refusal (m0466), and the red-line principle guaranteeing easy access to safety-critical information (m0018). Per policy a failed prediction obliges written justification and never auto-reverts; this revert is the designed outcome of the pre-registered bound, taken on the adjudications and on nothing else. No census number, panel score, judge rating or gold value informed this decision; census consultation stays deferred to the S8 checkpoint. WHAT THE CYCLE YIELDS — three findings, recorded as the cycle's real product: (i) CLAUSE_TAINT INHERITANCE. Patient-free atoms are discounted through sibling user-directed REMEDIAL acts, systematically mispricing example passages whose modeled response addresses the user while the harm falls on a third party. m0275's removal rests on taint imported from should_provide_supportive_response__model_user while the matched situation atom expressed_harmful_intent is glossed 'the user expresses an intention to harm another person'; m0466's on taint from the model-upon-user refusal act, which does not bear on who would be harmed by the requested advice; contested m0108 is the same shape. (ii) RECIPIENT-VS-HARM-BEARER. Protective acts UPON the user FOR others' benefit fire the mismatch rule against needed clauses — m0239's de-escalation act takes the user as grammatical patient while the harm it averts falls on people outside the conversation ('dropping it on the ground that the model's act is addressed to the user mistakes the recipient of the intervention for the bearer of the harm') — as do GENERIC-NOUN patients: m0018's 'People should have easy access to trustworthy safety-critical information' is annotated third_party, but 'people' as written comprehends the users and developers the model works with rather than excluding them, so the annotation reflects the clause's generic noun, not a subject matter foreign to helpfulness. (iii) WHAT WORKED, PRESERVED AS FINDING: patient-saturated wrong-patient clauses were correctly removed — m0276, the defining case, adjudicated `correct` exactly as pre-registered, and m0290 likewise; all 6 normalizer_drift admissions were adjudicated correct; and the golden-derived d = 0.10 with the taint cap behaved exactly as DISCOUNT_DERIVATION.md derived it (dense uniformly-mismatched clauses suppressed without the F-linearity residual; the flip set flat across the licensed range but for the one near-cut clause). THE DEFECT IS PATIENT PROVENANCE, NOT THE DISCOUNT ARITHMETIC: the pricing layer reads chains that record who an act is addressed to, and treats that as who the clause protects. These findings feed a pre-registered S3b REDESIGN — beneficiary-aware pricing (harm-bearer distinguished from act recipient) and no taint inheritance across act/situation siblings in example passages — which must pass its OWN design + adversarial review before any re-attempt; nothing from this cycle's mechanism ships in the meantime.
